STRUTTING

Strutting for Deep Excavations: A Buyer’s Guide

Understand the scope, interfaces and approvals behind an internal support system.

In this insight

See strutting as a systemCoordinate with the space belowMake time part of the scopePlan removal from the beginningFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

See strutting as a system

Strutting provides internal support within an excavation as part of an engineered arrangement. The commercial package may include members, connections, installation, inspections, adjustments and removal, but those inclusions must be stated. Buying steel alone is not the same as procuring a coordinated support package. Begin by asking what the proposal covers across the full period in which the support is needed.

Coordinate with the space below

Support locations interact with excavation equipment, material movements and construction of the permanent basement. Review the proposed arrangement with the teams responsible for those activities. The design authority must assess changes, but the delivery team can identify access conflicts early. A layout should be tested against the planned sequence rather than reviewed only as a static structural drawing.

Make time part of the scope

Clarify when support is required, how long it may remain and what assumptions underlie any hire or duration-based charges. Delays elsewhere can affect the commercial position even when the support contractor has completed its installation work. Ask how extensions, standby, damage, modification and staged removal will be treated. Clear terms reduce the chance that programme changes become avoidable disputes.

Plan removal from the beginning

Support removal is a designed transition, not simply the reverse of installation at a convenient moment. The relevant engineers must establish the conditions and approval route. Procurement should identify who coordinates that decision and what evidence is required. Including removal in the early programme helps the project team understand where the temporary and permanent works depend on one another.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Procure the support system, not just its steel.
  • Review access through the supported excavation.
  • Define duration and removal responsibilities.

References & further reading

  • Further reading: HSE — Temporary works (UK guidance)

International references provide technical context; applicable local requirements and the project engineer’s decisions govern the actual works.
